title: First trip to the Stuyvesant; how loud Bunk played
summary: Blumberg recalls arriving scared and hearing Bunk and Baby from half a block away, and compares Bunk's piercing volume to Kid Thomas.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What was the lie? Yeah, well, uh... first time I came, I was very young and kind of scared. It was the first time I was in a strange city by myself and, and, uh... I had received some kind of garbled directions of how to get at the Stuyvesant. And, uh, somehow I managed to... to get that, what was it? Second Avenue, I think it was on. But, uh... I remember, you know, wondering if I would ever find the place. And if I didn't, what would I do, you know? And, uh... Uh... I remember hearing the, the, uh, the music from a distance, just hearing, uh, bunk and baby as I, I guess, uh, crossed the street. I was probably half a block away from the, from the entrance of the Stuyvesant. And, uh... Uh, I could hear the trumpet and drums as I was approaching the place.
Well, that, by... My standards of present day New Orleans, that's not very loud, you know?
Well, I think maybe the, uh, the doors are heavier in New York and the walls thicker and so forth. Uh... But, uh, it was pretty loud. It was pretty loud. Well, say you're...

You know, when you're approaching Kid Thomas, did you have that experience of him playing across the street at Larry's place? And approaching that, it seems like you can hear him for further than any half a block.
But then he's playing right out into the open air.

Yeah, and, I mean, the doors were closed. This was in an enclosed, uh... I mean, when you walked into the Stuyvesant, you walked into a lobby, and there was a downstairs... There was a staircase, as I recall, and, uh, uh... Some kind of doorway straight ahead that I think went into the first floor hall. But anyway, as I remember, they were on the second floor, I believe, when they opened. And so you had to go up these stairs inside this lobby, and then, uh, you, uh, found the, uh, second floor hall, and it was kind of away from the street. It wasn't, uh...
You say Bunk played as loud as Kid Thomas does? You know, when he's playing at a peak?

Oh, I think louder. I think louder. Lighter than Kid Thomas? Well, yeah, I think Bunk had a more piercing, uh, uh, tone. I mean, it's hard for me to recall now, but he, I know he cut through. I know the band was a very loud band, and there were times when there was a lot of talk, and, uh, a lot of, there were a whole lot of people, there'd be a whole lot of people on the Stuyvesant, a whole lot of talk, and the band would be very loud, and Bunk would just cut through, uh, without, I mean, without any doubt at all. He just, uh, you'd hear every note anywhere in the place, just about.
